hed: A Quiet Morning on the Desk
deck: Table Rock this morning: 911.44 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Don't quit at 10.
play.body: Fall is the opposite of August. The bite can last until lunch.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 911.68 early in the week to 911.40 this morning — about 0.28 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Live USACE reading 12:00 CT: 911.40 ft, 7,775,295 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: The lake sits about 3.56 ft below full pool, exposing more shoreline, stumps, and hazards in shallow coves, upper arms, and near some ramps. Boaters should use extra caution, especially in the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms where navigation can tighten and docks may have limited access.

Surface water has cooled into the low- to mid-70s with excellent clarity in recent readings. Bass respond well to topwaters and soft plastics early in the day, then transition to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action continues with walleye holding on points in 20–25 ft and crappie or spotted bass coming from deeper brush and docks. Recent patterns show solid catches possible, though the low water means longer walks at certain launches and slower navigation in the upper arms.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~7,775,295 cfs at 12:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater stays productive year-round thanks to deep releases from Table Rock and steady stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: low or minimal flows early create prime windows for wading, light-line drifting, or indicator fishing with micro jigs, midges, and scuds, while stronger current (typically building later in the day) calls for weighted rigs and precise drifts through seams and behind structure.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, mega worms, or other soft plastics/scented baits for the water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent reports (Lilleys' Oct 1, John Sappington early Oct) highlight good rainbow numbers, strong brown activity (especially upper lake and first mile below dam), and success on marabou jigs (black, sculpin, olive), scuds, small streamers, midges, and night fishing with jerkbaits. Water clarity is excellent — clean presentations win. Night fishing has been particularly good for trophies. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before you wade or launch.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
